source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: Okay, please ensure it is a standard one that can be sourced easily. A simple test is whether it is available on AliExpress; if so, it is acceptable.

value_updates.component_selection_rule: Use a standard connector that can be sourced easily.
value_updates.sourceability_check: Availability on AliExpress is an acceptable sourceability test.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: That works, although this is a premium one costing 0.73$; they normally cost 0.20$. We can use this one as long as compatible alternatives exist in case it goes out of stock. My only concern is avoiding something that may not always be available.

value_updates.compatible_alternative_policy: A selected connector is acceptable only if compatible alternatives exist in case it goes out of stock.
value_updates.availability_priority: Avoid components that may not remain consistently available.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
There are also many Extended components with a $3 setup fee, meaning I need to pay $44 only for setup, even for resistors and capacitors. Please look at the image.
Could this be because we are using a non-standard size, such as 0603 vs 0805, or something similar? I expected that for AXP, but it seems strange for capacitors and resistors. What is your opinion?

execution.observed_behavior: JLCPCB classified many components, including ordinary resistors and capacitors, as Extended components, resulting in $44 of setup fees.
The selected sensor-board connectors were unavailable for assembly.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: Hi, could you please check the parts cart? I received an email saying that the price of this part changed and the minimum order is 20pcs. However, the 6-pin version costs 1.28 per piece, while the 8-pin version is 0.28. I don't understand why that is. Can you check whether there is an alternative and what we could do? Otherwise, I would need to pay almost $30 for just one type of connector.

execution.observed_behavior: A selected connector developed a 20-piece minimum order and a high unit price, creating an almost $30 procurement cost for one connector type.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: If there is no other option, I can simply order them, although the cost is around 10% of the total for all the boards :)

value_updates.high_moq_connector_fallback: If no suitable alternative exists, purchasing the connector at the required minimum quantity is acceptable.

source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text: The components in the bom have now been replaced.

execution.observed_behavior: The freelancer reports replacing BOM components following the missing-component report.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: It appears that those have also gone out of stock in the meantime.

execution.observed_behavior: After the component-replacement claim, the two main-board connectors were found to have gone out of stock.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: Ok, so ordering it this way is fine. If they are inexpensive, we can include them as well.

value_updates.optional_main_board_connector_policy: The optional ESP32-adjacent connectors may be left unassembled when unavailable; include them when inexpensive.

routing_warnings.description: The proposed division of the hard-to-source 13-pin connector into separate power and signal connectors primarily changes the interboard interface architecture.
The duplicate part number assigned to capacitors with different values is a BOM accuracy issue rather than a component-sourceability transition.
The statement that the sensor board lacks the connectors concerns connector implementation on that board, not merely sourcing availability.
